question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` plus the two new `agent-harness-runtime` helper exports as the public ContextEngine/SDK contract now, or fold this into the broader assemble metadata RFC #82137?
rationale: This changes a plugin-facing API surface and creates durable third-party expectations; automation can verify mechanics, but it cannot choose the intended permanent ContextEngine contract.

options.title: Approve Narrow API After Fixes
options.body: Accept this PR's API direction after the count/message mismatch, generated artifacts, and live proof gaps are resolved.

options.title: Fold Into RFC #82137
options.body: Pause or close this PR and handle token counts alongside the broader assemble provenance/internal-event metadata design.

options.title: Accept Current Risk
options.body: Merge the narrow contract now despite missing live proof and generated-artifact blockers, leaving follow-up work to harden the surface.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow API After Fixes
recommendation.body: Accept this PR's API direction after the count/message mismatch, generated artifacts, and live proof gaps are resolved.
